I agree that looking at facts is best... But look at all of them, not just a few. The .223 round is regulated and tested by SAAMI. So yeah, SAAMI says that the pressure is 55kpsi. The 5.56 is a NATO spec round, so they define the pressure. That's defined by a process called EPVAT. It is a different testing technique (different position of the pressure sensor) that what SAAMI uses. The EPVAT method does result in exactly the numbers that you mention, 62kpsi.

But, NATO has also used a newer standard called SCATP. This testing methodology is designed to largely mimic the SAAMI standard pressure test. The 5.56 round using the SCATP test gives the pressure at 55kpsi.

The exact same 5.56 round with the EPVAT test gives the pressure at 62kpsi, and the exact same 5.56 round using the SCATP test (which is similar to the SAAMI test) gives the pressure 55kpsi. That's because EPVAT and SCATP and two different testing techniques.

What did you just say the .223 pressure was? 55kspi. That's the same as the NATO SCATP test.

Don't take my word for it. Look at the Wikipedia article for 5.56 and search for SCATP.

Of course I'm not claiming that the rounds are interchangeable. There are differences in bullet position, throat length, chamber shape, etc. But the difference in pressure is overblown.
